author: k. p. rodriguez
title: Muncy Place ranked 3rd among Lycoming County nursing homes in Q1
text:
Muncy Place was the third largest nursing home in Lycoming County in the first quarter of 2026, data from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) shows .
The facility offered 138 beds, surpassing the Lycoming County average by four as measured in the first quarter of 2026. On average, it served 100.9 residents throughout that time frame.
CMS granted Muncy Place an overall rating of 3 out of 5, matching the statewide average rating for Pennsylvania nursing homes.
Valley View Rehab and Nursing Center was the county’s largest nursing facility during the quarter with 163 beds, while Edenbrook North placed second, offering 152 beds.
As of the opening quarter of 2026, Muncy Place reported no fines or penalties from state or federal health authorities.
There were three non-profit nursing homes recorded within Lycoming County, Pennsylvania.
Estimates from the U.S. Census Bureau indicate that the nation’s population of older adults continues to rise as the number of children dwindles. Between 2020 and 2024, there was a 13% increase in people age 65 or older, even as those under 18 fell by 1.7%. Over the last century, America’s older adult population has expanded sharply , climbing from 4.9 million in 1920 to more than 61 million in 2024.
A 2021 brief projected that nearly half—around 28 million—of Americans in this age group might need long-term support and services. The report also estimated that more than one-third will eventually require care in a skilled nursing setting.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , who is executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
